summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Queen's Park Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 414/8 (153.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 185/10 (55.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: BKG Mendis 102 (210b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, D Bishoo delivered a masterclass for West Indies (56 Runs & 5 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (West Indies 45%) and allowing West Indies to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. West Indies's bowling unit, bolstered by CBRLS Kumara (8 Runs & 7 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing West Indies won by 226 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: West Indies's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, West Indies won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
